proposedPublicPatch.title: Houston: check the unit’s permitted use before committing rent
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Houston commercial lease: Certificate of Occupancy and use
proposedPublicPatch.description: Request the occupancy record for the exact Houston unit and compare your proposed work before relying on a landlord’s commercial-space description.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: A bay previously used by a business is not necessarily suitable for your planned storage, equipment or customer access. Establish the actual City of Houston unit and its authorised use before building a lease or opening date around it.

sections.heading: What the reviewed city guidance establishes
paragraphs: The city business page says a Certificate of Occupancy (CO) is required before a commercial building or individual lease space is occupied, or when its occupancy classification changes. Obtain the current record and compare it with the proposed activities, layout and alterations.
Describe relevant storage, chemicals, powered equipment and public access. The city lists building, fire, food and other reviews, but that does not make every permit mandatory for every business.

sections.heading: What to establish before relying on the space
paragraphs: Check the parcel, address and unit: the Houston metro, Harris County and City of Houston are not interchangeable. A mailing address or landlord’s account of the previous tenant does not settle the responsible authority or proposed use.

Resolve the applicable occupancy and inspection questions before relying on the date at which rent, equipment orders or customer promises create costs. You may model a delay to understand exposure, but it is not the city’s promised timetable or a legally required lease clause.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Obtain the exact unit’s current CO and ask which approvals your proposed use requires before relying on the lease/opening plan.
limitations: This is a pre-lease occupancy check from a city summary. Detailed official permitting PDFs were access-blocked; current application steps, fees, classification outcome and parcel approval remain unverified.
Actual building, fire, environmental and sector conditions need their own answer.

proposedPublicPatch.title: Indianapolis extinguisher work: the company and each person need checking
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Indianapolis extinguisher company and service-person licences
proposedPublicPatch.description: Check the local business and each extinguisher technician’s licensing and certification; the workshop’s construction-completion question is separate.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: Do not dispatch the whole team on the strength of one company document or one technician’s credentials. The reviewed Indianapolis process identifies both the business and each service person.

sections.heading: The named service needs both checks
paragraphs: The city guidance calls for a business licence and each service person’s licence for the named fire-prevention equipment service. Individual applications also need the Indianapolis Fire Department’s certification stamp. The linked forms concern fire-extinguisher servicing, not automatic permission for alarms, sprinklers, sales, installation or every maintenance task.

The company and individual applications identify the actual local business and associated person. Brand training or the overseas parent’s licence does not establish those permissions. The city’s current published page still links applications marked October 2023. Confirm the applicable fees, certification steps and licence terms; the separate signed 2026 premises letter does not update those licensing terms.

sections.heading: If the workshop also has construction work
paragraphs: The signed 2026 city/county letter says it does not currently issue a Certificate of Occupancy. For covered construction it describes the permit holder’s Certificate of Completion and Compliance within 14 days after completion AND before occupancy or use. Those are both conditions, not 14 days in which opening is allowed.

A stated structural-permit exception depends on a registered architect or engineer properly filing the specified certificate. The separate fee trigger 30 days after permit expiry is not an opening grace period. Check whether the actual parcel is in the consolidated jurisdiction or an excluded municipality.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Confirm the correct company permission and each proposed technician’s certification/licence before offering the named extinguisher service.
limitations: Administrative guidance and dated linked forms only; current ordinance scope, insurance/storage/environmental requirements and work outside Indianapolis remain unchecked.
The premises letter concerns 2026; current fee/renewal terms, actual permit exception and excluded-municipality boundary remain unresolved.

proposedPublicPatch.title: Dallas: taking over the same-use unit can still mean a new CO
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Dallas Certificate of Occupancy for a new tenant
proposedPublicPatch.description: Dallas lists tenant change as a new-CO trigger. Check the exact unit and proposed operation rather than relying on the previous tenant’s certificate.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: A landlord’s assurance that the broad use is unchanged does not settle the incoming Dallas tenant’s occupancy task. Dallas lists tenant change separately from a change in use.

sections.heading: Which fact changed?
paragraphs: The official page lists first use, tenant change on an existing CO, changed use and changed floor area among new-Certificate-of-Occupancy triggers. Obtain the previous CO for the exact unit and describe the incoming company, work, equipment, storage and area.

The page directs applications through DallasNow, but the applicable application, inspections and multi-tenant prerequisites still need confirming for the proposal. Do that before scheduling customer work on the assumption that the former tenant’s document is yours.

sections.heading: If only the trading name changes
paragraphs: Dallas’s page describes a conditional record-change route near the start and a standalone-application description later for a DBA-only change. DBA means “doing business as”. That current workflow remains unresolved: confirm it with Dallas before relying on a shortcut or fee.

A trading-name change and a different legal tenant are not automatically the same event. A chosen rent-delay allowance can help assess cash exposure, but it is not the city’s promised completion time or a required lease term.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Obtain the exact unit’s CO and confirm the incoming tenant’s applicable city process before relying on an opening date.
limitations: Narrow Dallas occupancy guidance only. Actual fees, inspection outcome, other premises/trade duties and full employment/tax/franchise requirements remain unverified.

proposedPublicPatch.title: Dallas or San Antonio: the same-use takeover can differ
proposedPublicPatch.seoTitle: Dallas versus San Antonio CO routes for a tenant change
proposedPublicPatch.description: The two cities describe different occupancy-certificate treatment for an incoming operator. Use the city guides for the actual proposal.
proposedPublicPatch.learningSummary: An existing workshop and an unchanged broad service do not guarantee the same occupancy task in Dallas and San Antonio.

sections.heading: The difference worth checking
paragraphs: Dallas lists tenant change on an existing Certificate of Occupancy (CO) as a new-certificate trigger. San Antonio describes an update for certain owner/lessee changes with essentially the same use, but listed categories still need a new certificate. Both describe new-CO requirements for changed business use.

A name-only change is another question. Dallas’s current page has conflicting record-change and stand-alone application descriptions, so its DBA-only workflow and fee remain unresolved. San Antonio’s linked DBA (doing business as) name-change form requires fire review and inspection for specified uses, including repair and maintenance shops, and applies the COO-No Construction fee category. An update is not a promise of no inspection or a lower charge.
Request the prior CO and actual operator/use facts for the chosen unit, then continue with that city’s guide. This comparison cannot choose a use classification, inspection route or opening date.

proposedPublicPatch.practicalOutput: Use the chosen city’s guide to confirm its actual tenant/use route before relying on the former operator’s CO.
limitations: Two-city comparison only, not a Texas-wide rule. Actual site/use, construction/fire/trade conditions and the unresolved Dallas name-only workflow remain; no shortcut, numerical fee or timing advantage is established.
